clue.text: One right in the head, but a bad sailor?

indicators.note: 'in' tells us the pair of letters sits inside the word for the head

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone with a sound mind who is nonetheless hopeless at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One right in the head' sounds like a sane person; it is I and R placed in PATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer is a sailor, but a wicked one, so 'bad' does double moral duty with the question mark.

clue.text: Strip for 6 set — a pun's involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter; the 's here reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A newspaper comic strip about a bird is built around a piece of wordplay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges SET plus APUN. Woodstock (6 down) is the little yellow bird in Charles Schulz's comic strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Schulz's long-running comic strip features Snoopy's bird companion, so it is the strip for that bird.

clue.text: Odd beat regularly used for dance

parts.note: rum is a dated British word for odd or strange

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word beat

explanation.surface: An unusual rhythm, kept steady, is used for dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the first and third letters of 'beat', giving BA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance in four-four time, so it is one kind of dance.

clue.text: Rock band coming in to look for guitar effect

indicators.note: coming in tells us the group enters the middle of the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
R.E.M. is an American rock band
lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: A rock group arrives to check out a sound effect on the guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' is the container signal; R.E.M. are an American band, and 'lo' is the archaic exclamation 'look!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trembling, rapidly repeated effect, produced on guitars by a whammy bar, is a classic guitar effect.

clue.text: 6 act cut in two — hospital for one week

indicators.note: 'for one' says the hospital letter takes the place of one of the week letters
'in' puts the word for cut inside the word two

parts.note: to hew is to cut with an axe
H is the abbreviation for hospital on road signs and maps

explanation.surface: A band at the festival is split up, with a hospital stay of a week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the word for cut inside TWO, giving THEWWO; 'for one' then swaps the hospital letter for one of the two W's. The Who played at Woodstock.
explanation.definitionFit: The British rock band played a famous set at the 1969 festival, so it was one of its acts.

clue.text: Surely not a 6 theme? That ingratitude's showing!

indicators.note: showing means the letters can be seen inside the words That ingratitude

explanation.surface: Someone protests that such ungratefulness is clearly on display.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap between 'That' and 'ingratitude'. The festival's themes were peace and love, so this feeling was surely not one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing is the opposite of the love and peace the festival stood for, so it is surely not a theme.

clue.text: Bird drawn on top of family trees?

indicators.note: in a down answer, the piece written first sits on top of the piece after it

parts.note: a wood is a collection of trees
stock means ancestry or family line

explanation.surface: A bird perched on top of a family tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn' means sketched: the bird is a cartoon one, Snoopy's friend in the Peanuts strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Schulz's comic strip has a little yellow cartoon bird of this name, a bird that is drawn.

clue.text: Increasing paperwork when producing the Animals and the Byrds, say

definitions.text: Increasing paperwork when producing the Animals and the Byrds, say

parts.words: Increasing paperwork when producing the Animals and the Byrds, say
parts.note: read 'Increasing' as 'in creasing': folding sheets of paper into animal and bird shapes; the two 1960s band names sound like the creatures

explanation.surface: Admin keeps growing when managing the bands the Animals and the Byrds.
explanation.walkthrough: The Animals and the Byrds were 1960s bands, but read as creatures (Byrds sounding like birds) they are what Japanese paper folding produces.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese paper folding is literally paper work in creasing, often making models of animals and birds.

clue.text: Big-headed girl — expert on the penis, we hear

parts.note: Meg is a girl's name

indicators.note: we hear tells us the phrase is to be said aloud and spelt as it sounds

parts.note: an ace (expert) on the phallus (penis) gives ace-phallus, said aloud

explanation.surface: A conceited girl is a specialist in male anatomy, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big-headed' looks like conceit but is meant literally: having a large head.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek-derived medical term means having an abnormally large head, literally a big head.

clue.text: See 19
Like emails chosen by guy in charge

parts.note: elect means chosen, as in the president-elect
Ron stands for any man's name

explanation.surface: A man in charge is picked out, perhaps by email.
explanation.definitionFit: Emails are sent by computer, so they are digital in nature.

clue.text: Varying of tempo in first half of a troubadour's playing

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first half of takes the opening five letters of the ten-letter word

explanation.surface: A medieval minstrel's performance changes speed partway through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first half of' takes TROUB; 'playing' rearranges A + TROUB.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, a flexible speeding up and slowing down for expression is a varying of tempo.

clue.text: I forget faceless names, including name at 1 across

indicators.note: faceless means the word names loses its first letter, its face
including means the next letter goes inside the trimmed word

parts.note: the Roman numeral for 1 is I
AC is the crossword abbreviation for across

explanation.surface: Someone admits forgetting names that lack faces, even the one at the first clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faceless' drops the first letter of the word names and 'including' puts N in the remainder. 'I forget' is what someone with memory loss says, so the phrase stands for the person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with memory loss might well say 'I forget', so the phrase stands for such a person.

clue.text: Mental disorders causing tenor to quit film sets

parts.note: Psycho is Hitchcock's 1960 film

indicators.note: to quit tells us a letter leaves the combined letters

parts.note: taken as written
T is an abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: Psychological problems make a singer walk off the film set.
explanation.walkthrough: PSYCHO + SETS with 'to quit' taking T out.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe mental illnesses involving a loss of contact with reality are mental disorders.

clue.text: Soccer game about to finish as Italian added to score?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the next word
game here means willing to be reworked, so the letters of Soccer are rearranged

parts.note: end means finish

explanation.surface: A football match is about to end, as an Italian joins the scoresheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' scrambles the football word and 'about' puts it round the word for finish. The score is a musical one, not a match result, and Italian supplies most musical directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical directions on a score are usually in Italian, and this one means getting gradually louder.

clue.text: Jimi Hendrix's first cello tune, oddly arranged for 6's writer

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, as music is arranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of Hendrix

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: oddly takes the first and third letters of the word tune

explanation.surface: A guitar legend's tune is strangely rearranged for cello, for the composer of a festival song.
explanation.walkthrough: JIMI + H (first of Hendrix) + CELLO + TN (odd letters of tune) are rearranged. The Canadian singer wrote the song 'Woodstock'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canadian singer-songwriter wrote the song named after the festival, so she was its writer.

clue.text: Young person getting 10 out of 10

indicators.note: getting means the number word takes in the letter

parts.note: the plain number ten, spelt out
10 across is electronic, abbreviated E as in email

explanation.surface: A youngster scores full marks.
explanation.walkthrough: The second '10' points to 10 across, ELECTRONIC, abbreviated E as in e-mail; 'getting' has TEN take it in, and 'out of' just links. The surface's perfect score is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent between thirteen and nineteen is a young person.

clue.text: Stands model right on top of 10 music players

indicators.note: in a down answer the earlier pieces sit on top of the later ones

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
iPods are electronic (10 across) music players

explanation.surface: A model is positioned upright on top of some music devices.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-legged supports for cameras and the like are stands.

clue.text: They'll switch cases, so one may arrive at Skye

definitions.meaning: keyboard keys that change letters between lower and upper case

definitions.text: so one may arrive at Skye
definitions.meaning: read as an instruction, shift the letters of keys and you reach the island of Skye

explanation.walkthrough: Skye is an island off western Scotland; rearranging 'keys' spells it.
explanation.definitionFit: Keyboard keys that toggle capitals change the case of letters, and moving 'keys' around produces Skye.

clue.text: Man eating cake — losing head, went crazy

indicators.note: eating means the man's name swallows the other letters

parts.note: Fred is a man's name

indicators.note: losing head means cake drops its first letter

explanation.surface: A man munches cake and then loses his cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops the C of the bakery item, giving AKE, and 'eating' puts that inside the man's name. 'Freaked' is period hippie slang, fitting the festival theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To freak out, in hippie slang, is to lose one's composure, or go crazy.

clue.text: Badly written, sugary type of writing at a jolly 6 venue

indicators.note: badly written means the letters are jumbled

parts.note: SF, science fiction, is a genre of writing
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: Poorly penned sentimental prose, fit for a cheerful festival setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly written' scrambles the sweet word with the science-fiction letters, giving YASGURSF. A 'jolly' is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Yasgur's dairy farm in Bethel, New York hosted the 1969 festival, so it was the venue.

clue.text: Repressed writer overturned set

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so in a down entry the word is read backwards

parts.note: to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: An author knocked over a group of things, holding back feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses PUT to give TUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotions that are held in and not expressed are bottled, or repressed.

clue.text: See 15
Pole dancing grips a southern city

indicators.note: grips means the rearranged letters hold the following ones
dancing means the letters of Pole move about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pole dancer clutches someone from the south of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' turns POLE into ELPO, which 'grips' A + S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Texan border town is a city in the United States.

clue.text: Exercise to serve as one theme of 6

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
an ace is a serve in tennis the opponent cannot touch

explanation.surface: Doing a workout to serve a cause at the festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodstock was billed as three days of love and harmony, so tranquillity was one theme.

clue.text: Crazed stick man of 4 hit

parts.note: Keith Moon was the drummer, wielding sticks, of the band at 4 across
struck means hit

explanation.surface: A drummer from the band hit something wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick man' is not a matchstick figure but a drummer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being driven mad by the moon is an old idea, so this adjective means crazed.

clue.text: One of 4 born together died lacking water

indicators.note: lacking means the letter for died goes missing

parts.note: one of quadruplets is a quad

explanation.surface: One of quadruplets has died without a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin for water appears in English words and is a crossword synonym for water.

clue.text: Reportedly like a prior friend of 6

definitions.meaning: a prior heard aloud is a 'prier', one who pries; being like that is being nosy
the beagle in the Peanuts strip, companion of the bird Woodstock

explanation.walkthrough: A prior is the deputy head of a monastery; heard aloud, the word is 'prier', a nosy person.
explanation.definitionFit: The beagle in Schulz's comic strip is the bird's best friend.

clue.text: Directors not right for dairy outlets?

indicators.note: not means the letter for right is removed

parts.note: rudders direct a boat's course

explanation.surface: Managers who are not right for a dairy shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk flows out of a cow's mammary glands, playfully called dairy outlets.
